Treaties are interpreted in good faith under Articles 31–33 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, starting from the ordinary meaning of their terms, read in context and in light of their object and purpose. Supplementary means, such as preparatory work and the circumstances of conclusion, serve only to confirm that meaning or to resolve an ambiguous or obscure text, or one that leads to a manifestly absurd or unreasonable result. The Convention binds states parties, and many states and tribunals also treat these rules as customary international law.

CONFIDENCE: 90
